keySource: The key is NYSED's own, read from the Map to the Standards in the released-items PDF and carried into provenance/itemmap_g8-2024.json by tools/extract_item_map.py. tools/merge_content.py re-checks every letter against that file item by item and refuses to build if one disagrees, so the key here cannot drift from the official table or be shifted by one released item. Every constructed-response answer below cites NYSED's own exemplary-response page and is checked against this project's transcription of the same item.

39.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 7 (PDF page 8)
39.check: A cone of radius 3 and height 5 has volume a third of pi times 9 times 5, which is 47.12. Both dimensions are in this item's figure and named in its long description.

40.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 12 (PDF page 13)

41.check: From A at negative 1, negative 4 to B at 4, 8 is 5 across and 12 up, and 5-12-13 is a Pythagorean triple. The endpoints are in this item's figure.

42.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 22 (PDF page 23)
42.check: Angle ABC is 180 minus 110, which is 70, and angle ACB is 180 minus 105, which is 75, leaving 35 for angle BAC. Both marked angles are in this item's figure.

45.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 52 (PDF page 53)

46.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 62 (PDF page 63)
46.check: Three quarters of 3x minus 8, plus 4, equals 2x minus 8 gives x = 8. The equation is this item's own displayed expression.

47.answer: The square root of 49, 1.3 repeating, seven halves and 1.234 are rational; the square root of 32 is irrational
47.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 72 (PDF page 73)
47.check: 49 is a perfect square and 32 is not; a repeating or terminating decimal and a fraction of integers are all rational. The list is in this item's figure.

48.check: Store A charges $3.50 a yard and Store B $2.75, so nine yards cost $31.50 and $24.75. Store A's equation is in the stem and Store B's rate is read from its graph.
